comments.author: ismailmaj
comments.story: Ask HN: What Are You Working On? (February 2026)
comments.why: Incentives backfire for creative white collar work
comments.text: How do you scale a more human management system when both the manager or the managee can be incompetent or malicious. I'm aware that incentives are often counterproductive or insulting for white collar workers where there are elements of creativity in the job, but I feel like to get it to work you need trust which IMO cannot be scaled to big companies like Google. FYI, I'm paraphrasing, perhaps badly "The puzzle of motivation | Dan Pink | TED". [VIDEO]

comments.author: DeepDuh
comments.story: Why did a Train Carrying Biofuel Cross the Border 24 Times and Never Unload?
comments.why: Traditional incentives are less effective for creative work
comments.text: Traditional incentives are often not as effective as you think: [VIDEO] The best way to have motivated employees for creative tasks is to give them a high base salary, good working conditions and hire suiting ones in the first place. For repetitive jobs the incentives might work, but these are also the jobs where you should think about automation.
